name: Better Jobs Ontario (funded retraining for laid-off or long-unemployed people)
summary: Ontario grant that can cover tuition, books, transportation and a basic living allowance while an eligible laid-off or long-unemployed person trains for an in-demand job.
what_you_do: With an Employment Ontario provider, you research an in-demand occupation and an approved training program, then build and submit an application. If approved, you attend the training while Better Jobs Ontario helps with costs, then look for work in that field.
who_it_may_fit: You live in Ontario, were laid off (or have been unemployed 12+ weeks in a low-income household) and want funded training for a new occupation.
Up to $28,000 for training of 1 year or less, or up to $35,000 for programs over 1 year and up to 2 years
Basic living allowance up to $500/week plus a transportation allowance (guidelines cite $45/week)
May also cover childcare, disability-related supports and language training
People receiving EI, Ontario Works or ODSP can still apply
Not laid off? You may still qualify after 12+ weeks unemployed in a low-income household
who_it_may_not_fit: You need wages right away, would have to quit a current job to train, or are not a citizen or permanent resident.
Must be an Ontario resident and a Canadian citizen or permanent resident (program guidelines)
Living allowance is income-tested and only tops household income up to a 'moderate standard of living'
Quitting a job less than 12 months ago can make you ineligible unless the quit is authorized
Training for regulated occupations must be fully accredited
Multi-step application that colleges say can take several months; some college pages still cite older rules (e.g., 6 months unemployed)
No first-hand accounts of approval times found in this research pass
audience_restriction: People in Ontario who were laid off or have been unemployed for a long stretch

conditions_notes: Allowance paid during approved training; job outcomes after training not evidenced.
Approved costs (tuition, books, transportation, other instructional costs) covered up to the caps; costs above caps not described in sources found.

economics_notes: Allowance, not wages: up to $500/week basic living allowance plus $45/week transportation (EOPG guidance), income-tested.
